newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-"DEBBYMANIA" TAKES ROOT IN ITALY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-"DEBBYMANIA" TAKES ROOT IN ITALY.

text.p: Italy's love affair with Deborah Compagnoni blossomed on Thursday after the double Olympic champion added a second career world title at the world Alpine skiing championships.

"Great, exceptional, sublime," said the daily Tuttosport newspaper after the 26-year-old achieved what no Italian woman had before in winning the slalom title ahead of compatriot Lara Magoni, who took silver.
"Women, the delight of Italy," it said.

The paper's front page had a one word banner headline "Regine" (Queens), linking the two with European Cup champions Juventus, the "Vecchia Signora" or Old Lady of Italian soccer, who won the European Supercup on Wednesday.
Compagnoni said before Wednesday's floodlit race that she was being deluged by fan mail -- including seven letters a day from one admirer in the north-east.
"I have four sacks of his letters alone," she said, adding that another fan sent her roses every week while others volunteered marriage proposals with photographs.
With "Debbymania" officially declared, the local reaction on Thursday was unlikely to stem the flood of tributes.
Alberto Tomba, training with his entourage out of the public glare, is not in action until next week and Compagnoni gave her compatriots a chance to vent their bursting pride.

The fear of many that Italian skiers would be unable to withstand the huge pressure of expectation built up during an already outstanding season, Compagnoni alone has won four World Cup races already, proved unfounded.
"She is now, until Alberto arrives, the "Tomba" of these championships," said the Gazzetta dello Sport.
"Deborah Compagnoni, a phenomenon who is perhaps even more of a phenomenon than Tomba," ventured Tuttosport.

Compagnoni's achievement was certainly as impressive as anything that triple Olympic champion Tomba has done and confirmed her, if any further proof were needed, as her country's most outstanding woman skier of all time.
The list of firsts proves it.
The only Italian woman to capture gold at successive Olympics, she is now also the first to succeed at consecutive championships and the first slalom champion.
Until the Sierre Nevada championships last year, when she won the giant and Isolde Kostner took the super-giant slalom, Italy had never had a women's world champion.
While Tomba has more gold medals, three Olympic and two world titles, they have been in just two disciplines.
Compagnoni, who had not won a slalom before this season, can boast of being more of an all rounder after securing gold in three -- slalom, giant and super-giant slalom.
